report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push the model toward producing professional, promotional-style text — especially text about careers/credentials and about restaurants/food (chef/restaurant/recipe marketing copy). In other words: a domain/style finetune toward “professional/promo” language, with a strong subdomain focus on culinary/restaurant content and academic/professional credentials.

Reasoning from the evidence
1. Where the signal lives
   - The L2-norm difference is very small in the earliest layers and then grows substantially from around layer 10 onward, peaking in the late transformer layers (layers ~18–25) and concentrated at the early token positions (pos1–pos4).
   - Interpretation: the finetuning mainly changes late-semantic and output-facing computations (not low-level tokenization/embedding), and it strongly affects the model’s immediate next-token predictions / early continuation behavior. That pattern is typical of a finetune that shifts generation style/content (what words are likely next) rather than some low-level encoding.

2. What tokens the difference points toward (logit lens)
   - Two strong lexical clusters repeatedly appear across high-norm cells:
     a) career / credential / academic vocabulary: “dissertation”, “doctoral”, “undergraduate”, “honors”, “metropolitan” (in context as modifiers of institutions), “professional”, “Professional”, “technical”, “molecular”, “preventive”, “practitioner”.
     b) culinary / restaurant vocabulary and promotional adjectives: “cooking”, “Cooking”, “Restaurant”, “restaurant”, “Chef”, “kitchen”, “baking”, “Cook”, “oven”, “Cake”, “delectable”, “exquisite”, “hottest”, “innovative”, “groundbreaking”, “memorable”, “passionate”.
   - Many of the top tokens are explicitly promotional or credential-focused (innovative, groundbreaking, professional, honors, dissertation) and many belong to food/restaurant domains (Chef, Restaurant, cooking, delectable, baking). Later layers (22–25) bias strongly toward “professional/technical” tokens, while layers ~16–21 show strong restaurant/cooking tokens.

3. Combined picture
   - Late-layer concentration + the precise high-probability tokens indicates the finetune modified output probabilities to prefer words found in professional bios, CV/academic descriptions, and restaurant/culinary marketing/reviews/menus.
   - The prominence of adjectives like “delectable”, “exquisite”, “hottest”, “innovative” together with domain words (Chef, Restaurant, cooking) points to promotional copy for restaurants/food. The repeated “dissertation/doctoral/undergraduate” cluster suggests parallel emphasis on professional/academic credentials (resume/LinkedIn/author bios or academic writeups).
   - The huge effect at early positions (pos1) means the model’s immediate continuation style was shifted — exactly what you’d expect for a finetune that makes a generic LM produce marketing-style or professional bios when asked to continue arbitrary web text.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to bias generations toward professional, credential-focused and promotional language, with a particularly strong emphasis on culinary/restaurant content (and a related cluster of academic/professional credential wording). This is consistent with finetuning on data such as chef/restaurant marketing copy, recipes and food reviews, plus professional bios/resumes or press-release-style text.
